seo_title: ITAT Stays Rs 8,520 Cr Tax Demand on Singapore Govt
title: ITAT Mumbai Stays Rs 8,520 Crore Tax Demand on the Government of Singapore Over a Capital Gains Treaty Claim
case_name: Government of Singapore's capital gains tax demand on its India investments made through GIC
card_summary: The Mumbai bench of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal stayed recovery of about Rs 8,520 crore in tax demands on the Government of Singapore, a GIC-managed investor in India, for AY 2022-23 to 2024-25. The department allowed the treaty exemption on dividend and interest income but denied it on capital gains, calling those gains commercial. The 180-day stay from 23 October 2026 leaves the exemption question undecided.
card_tip: A treaty exemption allowed for one kind of income, such as dividends, does not carry over to another, such as capital gains; expect the tax department to examine each income head on its own facts.
verification_notes: The Rs 8,520 crore figure (made up of Rs 3,345.94 crore, Rs 2,057.15 crore and Rs 3,116.96 crore for the three assessment years), the basis for denying the capital gains exemption, and the 180-day stay running from 23 October 2026 are reported consistently across Business Standard, The Federal and Equitypandit. The order is an interim stay and does not finally rule on the Article 22(2)(c) exemption question; only the stay is reported here, not a final outcome. This item serves the HNI/foreign institutional investor audience named in the firm's current research priorities (a sovereign investor's India tax dispute, reported through GIC as its fund manager).
